radial ice accumulations from a glaze to one tenth of an inch.

slippery travel conditions from freezing rain and drive carefully.

outages. The latest road conditions for the state you are calling

properties.areaDesc: Brevard, FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall across the upper St. Johns River has caused levels
near Cocoa to remain within Major Flood Stage, well above its
previous record flood stage. The river level trends will remain
generally steady near 18.5 ft or 18.6 ft through late week and into
the weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The crest has exceeded the previous flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:15 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 18.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:15 AM EST Tuesday was 18.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 18.6 feet
tomorrow morning.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.4 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf
Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, Significant coastal flooding
with up to 2.7 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National
Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast, Northern Monterey Bay
and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST
Wednesday. For the High Surf Warning, from midnight Tuesday
night to midnight PST Wednesday night. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, from 6 AM to 4 PM PST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.7 ft above normal (8.5 ft MLLW)
at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at
11:38 AM Thursday. The alignment of high surf and high tide will
increase the combined hazard significantly on Wednesday. These
predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge that will enhance the
astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90
minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through
the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 24 at 1:42PM PST until November 26 at 12:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait,
and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County.

* WHEN...Until 600 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 918 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides each day are forecast as follows (all times
local). MHHW is Mean Higher High Water, or the average
highest daily tide; MLLW is Mean Lower Low Water, or the
average lowest daily tide.
* Port Chicago: +2.5 ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu
11/26, +2.2 ft MHHW (7.1 ft MLLW) at 2:45 PM Fri 11/27, +1.7
ft MHHW (6.6 ft MLLW) at 3:44 PM Sat 11/28, and +1.2 ft MHHW
(6.1 ft MLLW) at 4:53 PM Sun 11/29.
* West Sacramento: +2.3 ft MHHW (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu
11/26, +2.1 ft MHHW (6.5 ft MLLW) at 6:02 PM Fri 11/27, +1.8
ft MHHW (6.2 ft MLLW) at 6:59 PM Sat 11/28, and +1.4 ft MHHW
(5.8 ft MLLW) at 8:03 PM Sun 11/29.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.5 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26,
+7.5 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/27, +7.3 ft at 6:00 PM Sat 11/28,
+6.7 ft at 9:00 AM Sun 11/29, and +6.3 ft at 9:00 AM Mon
11/30.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 6-8 feet, sets up to 10-12 feet along west-facing
beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, now through 1 PM PST
Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM today to 4 AM PST
Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the
time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 8
AM today to 10 AM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak through Thursday at 7.9-
8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set back in
late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain
around 3-6 feet this morning. A long period west swell arrives
late this afternoon and will bring elevated to high surf by
Thursday morning's high tide. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet
with local sets up to 10-12 feet on west-facing beaches. Surf
lowers to 5-7 feet by Friday morning's high tide.

will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

Thursday morning's high tide. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet
with local sets up to 10-12 feet on west-facing beaches. Surf
lowers to 5-7 feet by Friday morning's high tide.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns at Sanford
to reach Major Flood Stage. The river is forecast to continue to
climb through Major Flood stage through mid-week, remaining steady
around 8.4 feet through late week and into the weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Flooding becomes more significant to low
lying structures and marinas along the river in Volusia and
Seminole counties, including Sanford, Enterprise and Lake Monroe.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Tuesday the stage was 8.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Tuesday was 8.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.4 feet
tomorrow and will remain steady through late week and into the
weekend.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin will cause levels
on the St Johns River at Astor to rise through Major Flood Stage. The
river is forecast to slowly rise  through late week, reaching around
4.3 to 4.4 feet Friday and into the weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 4.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM EST Wednesday was 4.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 4.4 feet
early tomorrow afternoon.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 8 to 12 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the
Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected.
For the High Surf Warning, large damaging breaking waves of 15
to 22 feet with dangerous rip currents are expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST
Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Wednesday
to noon PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 AM
Wednesday to noon PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beaches (especially Oceano Dunes,
Pismo Beach, Morro Bay, and Guadalupe Dunes), roads, and
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers
(including Cayucos, Avila, and Pismo) and jetties. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Large breaking
waves may impact Morro Bay Harbor. Extremely high tides may
cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas
inside of harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 7.7-8.2 feet will
likely peak between 7am and 11am. Coastal Flood and High Surf
Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of the
respective warnings.

infrastructure.

morning.

the respective warnings if they are issued.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal
Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County
and Metropolitan Miami Dade.

* WHEN...Through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The last 30 days of rainfall has been 400 to 600 percent of
normal across portions of Palm Beach and Broward Counties, and
between 200 to 300 percent of normal across portions of
Miami-Dade County. This amount of rainfall has made the ground
very saturated over the east coast metro areas of South Florida,
and thus it will not take much rainfall to create exacerbated
flooding issues across the east coast metro areas.

Most likely amounts: 2-3 inches of rain.

Reasonable Worst Case (High-End): 4-6 inches of rain. A few
locations could see 10 or more inches of rain.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the Sacramento River, San Joaquin
River, and other Delta waterways in Solano, Yolo, Sacramento, and
San Joaquin Counties.


* WHEN...Until 600 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 944 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides each day are forecast as follows (all times
local). MHHW is Mean Higher High Water, or the average
highest daily tide; MLLW is Mean Lower Low Water, or the
average lowest daily tide.
* Port Chicago: +2.6 ft MHHW (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:01 PM Wed
11/25, +2.5 ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu 11/26, +2.2
ft MHHW (7.1 ft MLLW) at 2:45 PM Fri 11/27, and +1.7 ft MHHW
(6.6 ft MLLW) at 3:44 PM Sat 11/28.
* West Sacramento: +2.4 ft MHHW (6.8 ft MLLW) at 4:18 PM Wed
11/25, +2.3 ft MHHW (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu 11/26, +2.1
ft MHHW (6.5 ft MLLW) at 6:02 PM Fri 11/27, and +1.8 ft MHHW
(6.2 ft MLLW) at 6:59 PM Sat 11/28.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.5 ft at 3:00 PM Wed 11/25,
+7.4 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26, +7.3 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/27,
+6.9 ft at 6:00 PM Sat 11/28 and +6.2 ft at 7:00 PM Sun
11/29.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin will cause levels
on the St Johns River at Astor to rise through Major Flood Stage. The
river is forecast to slowly rise mid week, remaining steady around
4.3 to 4.4 feet through late week and into the weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Tuesday the stage was 4.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Tuesday was 4.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 4.4 feet late week,
remaining steady within Major Flood Stage through the weekend and
into early next week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

significant coastal impacts.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 24 at 1:27PM PST until November 25 at 1:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that flooding is occurring or
imminent. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 6-8 feet, sets up to 10 feet along west-facing
beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, through 1 PM PST Friday.
For the High Surf Advisory, through 4 AM PST Friday. Most
susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the
morning high tide, around 9 AM today and 10 AM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peaked this morning just under 8
feet. A long period west swell will bring high surf today, and
breaking waves may reach 6-9 feet with local sets up to 10 feet
on west-facing beaches. Surf lowers to 3-6 feet by Friday
morning's high tide.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 26 at 12:15PM PST until November 27 at 1:00PM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Duval
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents expected.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to 8 feet.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Duval County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 1 AM EST
Wednesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through late
Wednesday night. For the High Surf Advisory, from 11 PM this
evening to 3 AM EST Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Warning,
from 1 AM to 7 PM EST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 24 at 12:00PM EST until November 26 at 3:00AM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Southern Nassau
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1 foot of
inundation above ground level expected in vulnerable areas
near the waterfront and shoreline. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, 2 to 3, locally 3 1/2 ft of inundation above ground level
expected in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and
shoreline. For the Coastal Flood Watch, up to 2 to 3 ft of
inundation above ground level possible in vulnerable areas
near the waterfront and shoreline.

* WHERE...Southern Nassau County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 11 AM EST this
morning. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Thursday to
6 AM EST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Friday
morning through Friday afternoon.

* COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread moderate to locally major
flooding of vulnerable areas near the waterfront and
shoreline, including roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and
homes and businesses with basements near the waterfront.
Numerous road closures are likely, and vehicles parked in
vulnerable areas near the waterfront will likely become
flooded. Flooding will also extend inland from the waterfront
along tidal rivers and bays.

* SHORELINE IMPACTS...Breaking waves of 8 to 12 ft will result
in widespread beach flooding and dune erosion widespread beach
flooding and dune erosion during times of high tide. There is
potential for localized overwashes resulting in some flooding
of roadways and vulnerable structures behind protective dunes.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels are likely with
the Thursday morning and evening high tides, potentially
extending into the Friday morning high tides. This forecast will
be refined over the next 12 to 24 hours as timing of wind
forcing with respect to Thursday AM/PM high tides becomes more
clear. The forecast has been leaned towards a higher end water
level scenario to provide a bit of safety margin. If the timing
of strongest winds is quicker than currently forecast the peak
water level forecast could be increased by a few tenths for
Thursday morning. if slower the Thursday morning forecast could
be lowered slightly.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 26 at 1:25AM EST until November 26 at 11:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal
Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County
and Metropolitan Miami Dade.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The last 30 days of rainfall has been 400 to 600 percent of
normal across portions of Palm Beach and Broward Counties, and
between 200 to 300 percent of normal across portions of
Miami-Dade County. This amount of rainfall has made the ground
very saturated over the east coast metro areas of South Florida,
and thus it will not take much rainfall to create exacerbated
flooding issues across the east coast metro areas.

Most likely amounts: 2-4 inches of rain.

Reasonable Worst Case (High-End): 5-7 inches of rain. A few
locations could see 10 or more inches of rain.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Seattle has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain over the Olypics overnight plus an additional 2-4 inches
of rain, with snow levels well above mountain tops will drive the
Skokomish River above flood stage this afternoon to above Moderate
flood.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of
record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM PST Wednesday the stage was 15.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage this afternoon
to 17.9 feet late tonight. It will then fall below flood stage
late Friday morning. Further rises through the weekend are
likely, with exceeding flood stage possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 9:30AM PST until November 27 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

through flooded areas.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 8 to 12 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the
Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected.
For the High Surf Warning, large damaging breaking waves of 15
to 22 feet with dangerous rip currents are expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches. Highest surf and impacts likely
across west facing beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST
Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Wednesday
to noon PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 AM
Wednesday to noon PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beaches (especially Oceano Dunes,
Pismo Beach, Morro Bay, and Guadalupe Dunes), roads, and
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers
(including Cayucos, Avila, and Pismo) and jetties. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Large breaking
waves may impact Morro Bay Harbor. Extremely high tides may
cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas
inside of harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 7.7-8.2 feet will
likely peak between 7am and 11am. Coastal Flood and High Surf
Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of the
respective warnings.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 24 at 10:36AM PST until November 26 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

high peaks.

* WHERE...Southwestern Humboldt.

ridges and exposed coastal headlands.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High winds aloft along the Del Norte Coast

* WHAT...Tidal overflow flooding.

* WHERE...South Washington Coast.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PST Thursday during periods of high tide.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level,
during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near
bays, sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...For the South Washington Coast, total tides
at Toke Point will be 12.2 feet at 12 PM (Noon) PST Tuesday
November 24, 12.5 feet at 1230 PM PST Wednesday November 25, and
12.5 feet at 12 PM (Noon) PST Thursday November 26.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 24 at 12:49AM PST until November 26 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.instruction:

low-lying areas is expected due to high tides. Coastal residents

appropriate action to protect life and property.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Friday.

intensities could drive wet snow down to valley floors.

properties.instruction:

https://wsdot.wa.gov/travel

If travel is absolutely necessary, drive with extreme caution.
Consider taking a winter storm kit along with you, including such
items as tire chains, booster cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets
and extra clothing. Also take water, a first aid kit, and anything
else that would help you survive in case you become stranded.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southern San Francisco County in northern California...
Northwestern San Mateo County in northern California...

* WHEN...Until 230 AM PST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Ponding of water in urban or other areas is occurring or is
imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1124 PM PST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. This will
cause urban and small stream flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Daly City, South San Francisco, San Bruno, Pacifica, Burlingame,
Millbrae, Hillsborough, Brisbane, Colma, Broadmoor and Montara.
- Rainfall rates are between 0.25 to 0.75 inches per hour.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 24 at 11:25PM PST until November 25 at 2:30AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

dangers of flooding.

properties.areaDesc: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate coastal
flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6
to 11 feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until noon PST
Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beaches (especially from Santa
Monica to Palos Verdes and Malibu), roads, and structures.
Moderate beach erosion is possible. There is an increased risk
for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers
out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people
off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.
Extremely high tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage
over low lying areas inside of harbor areas (such as Naples in
Long Beach).

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An extreme high tide of 8.0 feet will peak
between 9 AM and 10 AM Thursday morning.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 25 at 2:14PM PST until November 26 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking
waves of 15 to 22 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High
Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 3 AM PST Thursday. For
the Coastal Flood Warning, until noon PST Thursday. For the
High Surf Advisory, from 3 AM Thursday to noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beaches (especially Oceano Dunes,
Pismo Beach, Morro Bay, and Guadalupe Dunes), roads, and
structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful
waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of
ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers
(including Cayucos, Avila, and Pismo) and jetties. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Large breaking
waves may impact Morro Bay Harbor. Extremely high tides may
cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas
inside of harbor areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An extreme high tide of 7.8 feet will peak
between 9 AM and 11 AM Thursday morning.
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 25 at 2:14PM PST until November 28 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other water side
infrastructure.

strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin will cause levels
on the St Johns River at Astor to remain steady with Major Flood
Stage between 4.3 and 4.4 feet.

forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 4.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Wednesday was 4.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain generally steady
between 4.3 and 4.4 feet through early next week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.

* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 6-8 feet, sets up to 10-12 feet along west-facing
beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, now through 1 PM PST
Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM Wednesday to 4 AM
PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the
time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7
AM today to 10 AM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak through Wednesday at 7.9-
8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set back
in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will
remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday morning, but a long
period west swell arrives Wednesday afternoon, bringing a
sharp increase to the surf for late Wednesday into Thursday.
Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with local sets up to 10
feet on west- facing beaches. Surf lowers to 5-7 feet by
Friday morning's high tide.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal
Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County
and Metropolitan Miami Dade.

* WHEN...From Tuesday evening through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The last 30 days of rainfall has been 400 to 600 percent of
normal across portions of Palm Beach and Broward Counties, and
between 200 to 300 percent of normal across portions of
Miami-Dade County. This amount of rainfall has made the ground
very saturated over the east coast metro areas of South Florida,
and thus it will not take much rainfall to create exacerbated
flooding issues across the east coast metro areas.

Most likely amounts: 1-3 inches of rain Reasonable Worst Case
(High-End): 4-6 inches of rain
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 26 at 11:12AM EST until November 27 at 1:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards...beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 6-8 feet, sets up to 10-12 feet along west-facing
beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, through 1 PM PST Friday.
For the High Surf Advisory, through 4 AM PST Friday. Most
susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the
morning high tide, around 9 AM today and 10 AM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides this morning will peak around 8
feet. A long period west swell will bring high surf today, and
breaking waves may reach 6-9 feet with local sets up to 10-12
feet on west-facing beaches. The higher surf will combine with
the morning high tides today to amplify coastal impacts and
erosion. Surf lowers to 3-6 feet by Friday morning's high tide.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 26 at 1:32AM PST until November 27 at 1:00PM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Southern Queens
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, two to three feet of
inundation above ground level in vulnerable areas near the
waterfront and shoreline. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up
to one foot of inundation above ground level expected in
vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline.

* WHERE...Southern Queens County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 6 AM EST Friday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6 AM to 1 PM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Severe flooding with extensive inundation of numerous
roads and buildings and extending inland from the waterfront and
shoreline, flooding homes and businesses and isolating some
neighborhoods. In some areas, battering waves may play a
significant role. Numerous roads will be impassable under
several feet of water and cars will be submerged. Some areas may
need to be evacuated.

* COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread moderate flooding of
vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline, including
roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and businesses
with basements near the waterfront. Numerous road closures are
likely, and vehicles parked in vulnerable areas near the
waterfront will likely become flooded. Flooding will also
extend inland from the waterfront along tidal rivers and bays.

* SHORELINE IMPACTS...Breaking waves of 5 to 9 ft will result in
widespread beach flooding and dune erosion during times of
high tide.

flooding will also extend well inland from the waterfront

structures as well.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working through the basin will cause river levels on
the St. Johns at Deland to continue rising through Major Flood Stage.
The river is forecast to reach its crest record of 6.3 feet this
weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM EST Wednesday the stage was 5.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 AM EST Wednesday was 5.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 5.9 feet.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 9:54AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

nws:urn:oid:2.49.0.1.840.0.7d864f6d0518b.title: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 9:54AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

properties.areaDesc: Northern Washington Coast; Grays Harbor County Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected. Inundation of 2.5 to 3.5 feet above ground
level is possible Tuesday along shorelines and low- lying
coastal areas. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves along the coast. For the first Coastal Flood Watch,
significant coastal flooding possible Wednesday with
inundation up to 2.5 to 3.5 feet. For the second Coastal Flood
Watch, significant coastal flooding possible Thursday with
inundation up to 2.5 to 3.5 feet.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast zone.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 8 AM to 3 PM PST
Tuesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 10 AM Tuesday to 4
PM PST Wednesday. For the first Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Wednesday afternoon. For the second
Coastal Flood Watch, from late Wednesday night through
Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Significant coastal flooding due to high tides and
storm surge is expected. This is expected to lead to numerous
road closures. Low lying property including homes, businesses,
and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Shoreline
erosion or damage may occur. Large breaking waves can knock
people off their feet, move driftwood and debris, and crash over
rocks and jetties. People can be injured or drown while
observing the ocean. Localized beach and coastal erosion is
expected.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 24 at 4:25AM PST until November 24 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

Never turn your back on the ocean and keep children and pets
close. Know the tides and forecast conditions. Follow warning
signs and respect barriers.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin will cause levels
on the St Johns River at Astor to remain steady with Major Flood
Stage between 4.3 and 4.4 feet.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Thursday the stage was 4.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EST Thursday was 4.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 4.4 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 25 at 2:55AM EST until November 27 at 1:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns Above Lake
Harney near Geneva to remain within Major Flood Stage. River levels
are forecast to hold near a crest through Wednesday before beginning
a very slow decline within Major flood stage later in the week and
into this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The river crest has surpassed its previous flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 10.8 feet, Water covers State Road 46 and it may
become impassable near Jungle Road and Prevatt Road. Standing water
on secondary roads near the river deepens to more than three feet
in some areas. Flooding becomes more significant to structures and
marinas from above Lake Harney to the Lake Jesup area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:30 PM EST Tuesday the stage was 13.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 3:30 PM EST Tuesday was 13.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 11.9 feet Tuesday,
December 01.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: Northern Washington Coast; Grays Harbor County Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves along
the coast. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected. Inundation of 3 to 4 feet above ground level
is possible Wednesday along shorelines and low-lying coastal
areas. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding
possible Thursday with inundation up to 3 to 4 feet.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County
Coast zones.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 PM PST Wednesday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 4 PM PST
Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Wednesday
night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Significant coastal flooding due to high tides and
storm surge is expected. This is expected to lead to numerous
road closures. Low lying property including homes, businesses,
and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Shoreline
erosion or damage may occur. Large breaking waves can knock
people off their feet, move driftwood and debris, and crash over
rocks and jetties. People can be injured or drown while
observing the ocean. Localized beach and coastal erosion is
expected.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 24 at 6:10PM PST until November 25 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

Never turn your back on the ocean and keep children and pets
close. Know the tides and forecast conditions. Follow warning
signs and respect barriers.

* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait,
and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County.

* WHEN...Until 400 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 856 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides forecast each day are (all times local
time):
* Port Chicago: 2.2 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 11:36 AM
Mon 11/23, 2.5 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 12:16 PM Tue
11/24, 2.6 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:01 PM Wed
11/25, and 2.5 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu
11/26.
* West Sacramento: 2.2 ft above normal (6.6 ft MLLW) at 2:49
PM Mon 11/23, 2.4 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 3:32 PM
Tue 11/24, 2.4 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 4:18 PM Wed
11/25, and 2.3 ft above normal (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu
11/26.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.4 ft at 2:00 PM Mon 11/23,
+7.5 ft at 2:45 PM Tue 11/24, +7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Wed 11/25,
+7.6 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131
* Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1

hazardous high wind event is expected or occurring in those areas
along the immediate coast. Many of the headland areas and beaches are

for individuals or high profile vehicles. The strong winds may also
cause property and/or tree damage. Sustained wind speeds of at least

sea cliffs.

profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Seattle has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain over the Olympics overnight with snow levels well above
mountain tops has driven the Skokomish River to major flood stage
this morning.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...From Wednesday, November 25 to Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:30 AM PST Thursday the stage was 17.9 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:30 AM PST Thursday was 18.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will fall below flood stage just after
midnight tonight to 15.7 feet late tomorrow evening. It will then
rise to 15.8 feet early Saturday morning. It will fall to 14.4
feet Sunday afternoon. It will then rise to 15.7 feet late Monday
evening. It will fall again and remain below flood stage.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8
feet on 03/19/1997.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

through flooded areas.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 830 PM PST.

evening. Freezing rain is occurring in these higher elevation
colder locations. Icy spots could develop. Use caution if out and
about driving or walking.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 6 to 11 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST
Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Thursday.
For the Coastal Flood Watch, Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of
sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas,
especially around the time of high tide, including over
beaches (especially from Santa Monica to Palos Verdes and
Malibu), roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is
possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Extremely high
tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low
lying areas inside of harbor areas (such as Naples in Long
Beach).

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 8.0-8.2 feet will
likely peak between 8 AM and 11 AM. An upgrade to a Coastal
Flood Warning would likely come by late today. Coastal Flood and
High Surf Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of the
respective warnings if they are issued.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 25 at 8:53AM PST until November 26 at 6:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Plan
for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait,
and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County.

* WHEN...Until 600 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 945 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides each day are forecast as follows (all times
local). MHHW is Mean Higher High Water, or the average
highest daily tide; MLLW is Mean Lower Low Water, or the
average lowest daily tide.
* Port Chicago: +2.6 ft MHHW (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:01 PM Wed
11/25, +2.5 ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu 11/26, +2.2
ft MHHW (7.1 ft MLLW) at 2:45 PM Fri 11/27, and +1.7 ft MHHW
(6.6 ft MLLW) at 3:44 PM Sat 11/28.
* West Sacramento: +2.4 ft MHHW (6.8 ft MLLW) at 4:18 PM Wed
11/25, +2.3 ft MHHW (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu 11/26, +2.1
ft MHHW (6.5 ft MLLW) at 6:02 PM Fri 11/27, and +1.8 ft MHHW
(6.2 ft MLLW) at 6:59 PM Sat 11/28.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.5 ft at 3:00 PM Wed 11/25,
+7.4 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26, +7.3 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/27,
+6.9 ft at 6:00 PM Sat 11/28 and +7.0 ft at 7:00 PM Sun
11/29.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131
* Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1

properties.areaDesc: Central Siskiyou County
properties.description:
* WHAT...The Wind Advisory is being replaced with a High Wind Warning
to match an expected increase in winds. For the High Wind Warning,
south winds 30 to 45 mph with gusts up to 65 mph expected.

* WHERE...Most of the Shasta Valley in central Siskiyou County. This
includes portions of Interstate 5 as well as the communities of
Weed, Gazelle, Grenada and Montague.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds could blow down trees, power lines, and
unsecured objects. Power outages are possible. Travel could be
difficult, especially for high profile vehicles.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highways and roads running west to east,
including highway 97, will be exposed to tough driving conditions
given the strong southerly wind speeds. Winds are expected to be
strongest late Tuesday morning through Tuesday afternoon.
properties.headline: High Wind Warning issued November 24 at 3:52AM PST until November 24 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

People are urged to secure loose objects, including large or

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Moderate to Major severity for the
following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain over the Olympics overnight with snow levels well above
mountain tops has driven the Skokomish River to major flood stage
this morning.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, the Skokomish River will cause major, near
record flooding throughout the Skokomish Valley. Deep and swift
flood waters will inundate residential areas, many roads including
SR 106, and much of the farm land.   Flooding will occur all along
the river including headwaters, tributaries, and other streams
within and near the Skokomish River Basin.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:30 AM PST Thursday the stage was 17.97 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 3:30 AM PST Thursday was 17.97 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 18.1 feet late this morning. It
will then fall below flood stage on Friday morning. Further rises
through the weekend are likely, with exceeding flood stage
possible.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8
feet on 03/19/1997.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the Sacramento River, San Joaquin
River, and other Delta waterways in Solano, Yolo, Sacramento, and
San Joaquin Counties.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 907 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides each day are forecast as follows (all times
local). MHHW is Mean Higher High Water, or the average
highest daily tide; MLLW is Mean Lower Low Water, or the
average lowest daily tide.
* Port Chicago: +2.5 ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu
11/26, +2.2 ft MHHW (7.1 ft MLLW) at 2:45 PM Fri 11/27, +1.7
ft MHHW (6.6 ft MLLW) at 3:44 PM Sat 11/28, and +1.2 ft MHHW
(6.1 ft MLLW) at 4:53 PM Sun 11/29.
* West Sacramento: +2.3 ft MHHW (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu
11/26, +2.1 ft MHHW (6.5 ft MLLW) at 6:02 PM Fri 11/27, +1.8
ft MHHW (6.2 ft MLLW) at 6:59 PM Sat 11/28, and +1.4 ft MHHW
(5.8 ft MLLW) at 8:03 PM Sun 11/29.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.5 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26,
+7.5 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/27, +7.3 ft at 6:00 PM Sat 11/28,
+6.7 ft at 9:00 AM Sun 11/29, and +6.3 ft at 9:00 AM Mon
11/30.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.

* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal

breaking waves of 8 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents.

feet with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until noon PST today.
For the High Surf Advisory, from noon today to 9 PM PST
Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beaches (especially from Faria
Beach to Silver Strand Beach), roads, and structures.

strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean

inside of harbor areas.

will peak between 9 AM and 10 AM Thursday morning.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain over the Olympics overnight plus an additional 2-4 inches
of rain, with snow levels well above mountain tops, will drive the
Skokomish River above flood stage this evening to above Moderate
flood.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM PST Wednesday the stage was 16.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 17.9 feet late tomorrow
morning. It will then fall below flood stage late Friday morning.
Further rises through the weekend are likely, with exceeding
flood stage possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 2:17PM PST until November 27 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1030 PM PST.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL FRIDAY AFTERNOON

properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

Flood Stage, reaching 6.2 feet late this weekend. Additional
rises are possible thereafter.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding with up to 2.7 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.
For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of
20 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...Pacific Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM to 4 PM PST
Wednesday. For the High Surf Warning, through midnight PST
Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tidal gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.7 ft above normal (8.5 ft MLLW) at
10:49 AM Wednesday and 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at
11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.

infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Del Norte; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides
will cause major flooding in low lying areas. Up to 1 foot of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying
areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood
Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf may cause major
flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood Coast. Up to 1.0
foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in
low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the
High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves up to 25 feet. Surf may
worsen coastal flooding along exposed beaches.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal
Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 1 PM PST
Wednesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 7 AM to 7 PM PST
Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Thursday morning
through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
These impacts will include, but not limited to sections of
Highways 101 and 1. Shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous surf
conditions and localized beach erosion. Beachcombing is highly
discouraged!.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The water levels from this are expected to
rival the water levels seen in January of 2026 that caused
significant coastal impacts.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 24 at 8:44PM PST until November 25 at 1:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that flooding is occurring or
imminent. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

These impacts will include, but not limited to, roadways in King
Salmon and the Arcata bottoms and sections of Highway 101.
Shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous surf conditions and
localized beach erosion. Beachcombing is highly discouraged!.

rival the water levels seen in January of 2026 that caused
significant flooding in King Salmon.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 24 at 8:44PM PST until November 26 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that flooding is occurring or
imminent. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding with up to 2.5 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker
waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 13 to 19 ft
expected.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 4 PM PST Thursday.

infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal
Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County
and Metropolitan Miami Dade.

* WHEN...Until 1 AM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The last 30 days of rainfall has been 400 to 600 percent of
normal across portions of Palm Beach and Broward Counties, and
between 200 to 300 percent of normal across portions of
Miami-Dade County. This amount of rainfall has made the ground
very saturated over the east coast metro areas of South Florida,
and thus it will not take much rainfall to create exacerbated
flooding issues across the east coast metro areas.

Most likely amounts: 2-4 inches of rain.

Reasonable Worst Case (High-End): 5-7 inches of rain. A few
locations could see 10 or more inches of rain.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: Seminole, FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns at Sanford
to reach Major Flood Stage today. The river is forecast to continue
to climb through Major Flood stage through mid-week, remaining steady
around 8.4 feet through late week and into the weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Flooding becomes more significant to low
lying structures and marinas along the river in Volusia and
Seminole counties, including Sanford, Enterprise and Lake Monroe.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 8.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:30 AM EST Tuesday was 8.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.4 feet
tomorrow evening.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: Brevard, FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall across the upper St. Johns River has caused levels
near Cocoa to remain within Major Flood Stage, well above its
previous record flood stage. The river level trends will remain
generally steady between 18.0 feet to 18.3 feet into the weekend and
early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The crest has exceeded the previous flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM EST Thursday the stage was 18.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:15 AM EST Thursday was 18.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 18.3 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 6-8 feet, sets up to 10-12 feet along west-facing
beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, through 1 PM PST Friday.
For the High Surf Advisory, through 4 AM PST Friday. Most
susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the
morning high tide, around 9 AM on Thursday and 10 PM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

erosion.

afternoon and will bring elevated to high surf by Thursday
morning's high tide. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with
local sets up to 10-12 feet on west-facing beaches. Surf lowers
to 3-6 feet by Friday morning's high tide.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, 1 1/2 to 2 1/2 ft of
inundation above ground level expected in vulnerable areas
near the waterfront and shoreline. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, 1 to 1 1/2 feet of inundation above ground level
possible in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline.

* WHERE...New York (Manhattan), Richmond (Staten Island) and
Kings (Brooklyn) Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Thursday to 6
AM EST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 8 AM to
noon EST Friday.

* COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread minor to moderate flooding
of vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline,
including roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and
businesses with basements near the waterfront. Numerous road
closures are likely, and vehicles parked in vulnerable areas
near the waterfront will likely become flooded. Flooding will
also extend inland from the waterfront along tidal rivers and
bays, including the Hudson River.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels are likely with
the Thursday morning and evening high tides. The forecast has
been leaned towards a higher end water level scenario to
provide a bit of safety margin. If the timing of strongest
winds is quicker than currently forecast the peak water level
forecast could be increased by a few tenths for Thursday
morning, and if slower the Thursday morning forecast could be
lowered slightly. Similarly if strongest winds linger later
into the evening, the Thursday evening water level forecast
could be a few tenths higher.
